findings.message:
Deletion races with publication

The owner scan and deletion are separate. A writer can publish a manifest/accounting row after the scan but before deletion; since the delete checks only the chunk versionstamp, it can remove a live capture's payload.

src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:213-215

Owner lookup defeats bounded bootstrap

Every chunk performs full accounting and manifest scans. The outer 32-entry budget does not bound these reads, so many retained captures and orphan chunks can make bootstrap prohibitively expensive and leave admissions unavailable.

src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:199-205

summary: Orphan reclamation meets the task, but owner detection is racy and unbounded.

evidence: The candidate deletes ownerless chunk rows with a versionstamp check in src/sentinel/replay-retention-bootstrap.ts:210-216.
The added test seeds an orphan chunk, completes bootstrap, and verifies stored_bytes is zero and the chunk key is absent in tests/sentinel-replay-bootstrap-retry.test.ts:101-115.
